newsitem.title: USA: Richard Jewell sues N.Y. Post, alleging libel.
newsitem.headline: Richard Jewell sues N.Y. Post, alleging libel.

text.p: Richard Jewell, the former Olympic bomb suspect, sued the New York Post on Wednesday, alleging the newspaper libeled him in a series of articles.

Lawyers for Jewell, who was cleared of suspicion last November in the bombing, said in a complaint filed in U.S. District Court in the Southern District that the articles, published in late July and early August 1996, included false and defamatory statements.
A spokesman for the Post had no immediate comment.
The lawsuit also cited an editorial cartoon that was allegedly false and defamatory, and a published photograph that falsely identified Jewell.

The complaint alleged one story falsely portrayed Jewell "as an individual with an aberrant and/or violent personality, and a bizarre employment history...who was guilty or likely guilty of criminal involvement" in the bombing.
The bombing, which remains unsolved, left two people dead and more than 100 wounded at Centennial Olympic Park in Atlanta last July.
From July to October, 1996, Jewell was under constant, intense scrutiny by FBI agents and the media.
The lawsuit alleged that Jewell was the "victim of a media attack...fueled and supported by the false and defamatory statements by (the N.Y. Post) and other media entities."

The lawsuit alleged Jewell suffered permanent injury to his reputation, "public hatred, contempt and ridicule" in a July 31, 1996 New York Post article which quoted W. Ray Cleere, president of Piedmont College in Demorest, Ga., where Jewell had worked as a security guard.
According to the lawsuit, Cleere later said the quotes attributed to him were false.
The suit also alleged that Jewell was "forever deprived of the deserved status of an individual who reacted properly to an emergency situation, and in so doing, saved many lives."
On July 27, 1996, Jewell first noticed an unattended package at the park that was later found to contain the bomb, and helped evacuate people from the area.
Jewell is seeking $5 million in compensatory damages and $10 million in punitive damages from the Post.
Several FBI agents were disciplined for their conduct in the investigation of Jewell.
Jewell reached legal settlements with CNN and NBC over their coverage of Jewell. A lawsuit against the Atlanta Journal-Constitiution, owned by Cox Enterprises, is pending.
The New York Post is owned by News Corp, Time Warner Inc owns CNN, and General Electric Co owns NBC.
